name: More Island Events
description: Adds new island events, written by the owner, to the ones the game draws from (more come in later versions). Four here: The Aspiring Adventurer -- a villager who loves to explore sees something glinting off the safe path. "Go investigate!" finds a pile of dirt, a stack of meat (food) or a golden chest of artifacts (tech points); half the time the adventurer gets home (with the find, or with a friend's help), half the time a trap leads to death (a grave) or a disappearance (no grave). "Stay on the safe path" brings them home 9 times in 10; otherwise they are lost: hurt, healed or disabled, a skilled survivalist, killed, gone, or they join another tribe. The event is rare and separate: it never takes a share of the game's own draw (the stock island events' chances never change); after a natural island event, Story / Cheat Upgrades' separate rare roll may bring one of these events (or an Isola Grand Event Collection event) between two natural ones, never in trouble and never in place of a rescue, and Pick Island Event can pick it; it comes as one of the villager encounters, never the village's first island event; it needs two villagers of 14 or more who are not nursing a baby and not the Golden Child, and the adventurer and the friend who may come to help are drawn from them. The reward is a random amount from the smallest to the largest food or tech-point gain of the game's own island events (200 to 1,500 food for the meat, 500 to 4,999 tech points for the chest); with Island Events Scale With Population or With Stored Food and Tech Points ticked, the amount scales as that patch scales the game's own events. Deaths are the game's own ("Unknown causes", with a grave); a disappearance is logged as one in the Deaths log. The popups show the owner's text in pages that fit the screen (OK shows the next) -- with Scrolling Popups installed, one scrolling popup for the question and one for each answer's result; the effects wait for the page that tells them, and the Island Events log keeps one entry for each event. And The Cave Explorers (A New Home only): once The Cave puzzle is done, two friends of 18 or more, at most 5 years apart, wonder what the cave hides. "Don't explore" changes nothing; "Explore the Cave" leads on: "Proceed Further" brings a scream in the dark (they run, then argue, make up, or both fall down a chasm and are gone for good, 1 in 10) or a find (a map that takes both away for good, 1 in 10; gold coins: tech points; a treasure map: three times as many; preserved food: twice the food); "Stay Here" lets them return what they found (food or tech points) or keep it (the researchers' tech points 8 times in 10; otherwise one or both die, with graves). Each award is a random amount from the smallest to the largest food or tech-point gain of the game's own island events (A New Home: 200 to 1,500 food, 500 to 4,999 tech points), scaled as the Aspiring Adventurer's is. And The Remembrance Ceremony and The Rumblings (all five games; one popup each, OK only). The Remembrance Ceremony needs at least one grave: everyone joins in -- children, nursing mothers and fathers, everyone -- each at the cemetery, "Honoring the Dead", and the feast quietly uses 10 food for every villager (never below 0). The Rumblings needs every puzzle solved and a finished hut: an earthquake damages each of the second and third population huts (the first, "The Hut", is a puzzle and is never damaged) one time in four (at least one always), each losing 10 to 100% of its building work; the builders must build it again (at 100% it is unbuilt again, as in a new village). Nobody is hurt; a village over its limit keeps everyone and has no new births until it is rebuilt. Each can come again. Pick Island Event lists each of these events and picks one whenever its own requirements hold (otherwise it says what the event needs). Off by default; Owner's Defaults ticks it. **Needs Story / Cheat Upgrades (on by default), which runs the rare roll and Pick Island Event; ticking this ticks it.** **Unverified in play: the event has not been seen in a running game** (emulated on the stock executable). The companion is "VVFP More Island Events.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; nothing is saved by it.
behavior_changes: The event is rare and separate: it never takes a share of the game's own draw (the stock island events' chances never change); after a natural island event, Story / Cheat Upgrades' separate rare roll may bring one of these events (or an Isola Grand Event Collection event) between two natural ones, never in trouble and never in place of a rescue, and Pick Island Event can pick it; it comes as one of the villager encounters, never the village's first island event. It can happen only while at least two villagers may go: 14 or more (280 age units), alive and present, not carrying a baby, and not the Golden Child; the adventurer and the friend of ending A8 are drawn from them, the friend never the adventurer.

Choice A, "Go investigate!": the find 50% a pile of dirt, 25% meat (a food award: 200 to 1,500 food), 25% a golden chest (a tech award: 500 to 4,999 tech points); then 50% a surviving ending (after the dirt A7 or A9; after a find A1, A5 or A8, which give the reward) and 50% a deadly one (A2 and A4 die, the game's own death with cause -1 and a grave; A3 and A6 disappear, no body), each equally likely within its half.

Choice B, "Stay on the safe path": 90% home safe; 10% lost, then 1 in 6 each: the healers (1 in 3 each: dies; a full recovery; health set to 10-50 and running disliked), joins another tribe (gone for good, no grave), a survivalist (+20 to 30 in Farming, Building, Research or Healing, at most 100), dies under a fallen tree, dies at the bottom of a cliff, disappears.

The reward is drawn, each amount equally likely, from the game's smallest to its largest stock island-event gain of that kind (src/vv_aspiring_adventurer.py AWARD_RANGES), and goes through the game's own food or tech writer; with Island Events Scale With Population or With Stored Food and Tech Points ticked, the amount scales as that patch scales the game's own events. The effects wait for their own page (the page that ends the ending's text), and the event writes its own one Island Events log entry; a disappearance is told to the Cause of Death companion (VvfpCauseVanishedBy), so its Deaths log records it as one.

The owner's words, by translation key (the event's popup shows the player's language when a translation has them), are laid out in pages that fit the game's popup -- whole paragraphs, else whole sentences -- each shown in turn with OK.

The Cave Explorers (A New Home): one more encounter like The Aspiring Adventurer (with both possible, each is 1 in m + 2), only while The Cave puzzle is done (world byte +0x9FA8) and two villagers who may go on The Aspiring Adventurer are 18 or more (360 age units) and at most 5 years (100 age units) apart; the pair is drawn among those ordered pairs. Three questions in the encounter dialog: the answers are given new words (the constructor's own text setter 0x4015A0) and centred again (the buttons' own size and move). Explore -> Proceed Further: 50% A (10% argue, 80% make up, 10% the chasm: both removed with no body), 50% B (10% a map: both removed with no body; 30% gold coins a normal tech award, 30% a treasure map 3x, 30% preserved food 2x food); Stay Here -> return (food or tech, 50/50, a normal award) or keep (50% the researchers' normal tech award, 25% name2 and name1 die, 25% name2 dies: health 0, a body and a grave). The effects wait for their own page: they are made when the page that ends the ending's text is shown, and the event writes its own one Island Events log entry with a Choice line for each answer clicked; each removal is told to the Cause of Death companion (VvfpCauseVanishedBy).

The Remembrance Ceremony and The Rumblings (ceremony_core.inc, ceremony_games.inc): each its own case past the island events' 15, the chooser's first answer only while it is due (the stock rand(15) otherwise, untouched), through two sites of its own; the game's own single-result popup shows the owner's words, the effects are made as it is built, with the event's one Island Events log entry. The Remembrance Ceremony: needs at least one grave (the game's own grave count); every living, present villager is started on its own through the game's own stop and action starter, as its Day of Honor starts each one (so no group filter leaves anyone out), at the cemetery, "Honoring the Dead"; the feast uses 10 food for every villager the game counts, never below 0 (Blessings Day's own rule). The Rumblings: needs every puzzle of the game's Puzzles screen solved and one of the second and third population huts (the first, "The Hut", is a puzzle and is never damaged) finished; each finished one rand(100) < 25 (none: one of them at random), each losing 10 + rand(91) percent of its building work, written as the states the game's own construction passes through (at 100% the new village's state).
explicit_non_changes: No executable byte is patched: the companion writes each site at run time, only after verifying every site's stock bytes (all of them, or none); without it the event does not exist.
Every stock event, its odds, the island-event timer and counting, the rescue rules and Custom Island Events are unchanged; nothing is saved by the companion.
evidence_status: implemented from exact-build disassembly; the draw, the popup pages, both choices' effects and the install with every other patch emulated on the stock executable in tests/test_aspiring_adventurer.py (The Cave Explorers: every path, its effects and its pages, in tests/test_cave_explorers.py); The Remembrance Ceremony and The Rumblings: the conditions, the draw, everyone sent and where, the feast, the damage and its states, the log entry and the words, in tests/test_ceremony_and_rumblings.py; runtime/player confirmation pending
